method: Behaviour cloning from four single-skill experts

expert_selection.criterion: Chosen by transition score, not by single-skill score. The full-budget handstand expert (5000 iterations) has identical solo metrics to the early one (1222 iterations) but its clone collapsed on jump->handstand (0.359 vs 0.953). The full-budget jump expert IS better solo (recovery 0.932 -> 0.970) and was kept, so the shipped pair gets both.

reference_protocol.note: The transition metric is window-dependent (the aggregate spans roughly 0.82-0.95 across window settings), so it only means anything together with this exact protocol. Compare challengers on these commands and nothing else.

robustness.note: measured with the shorter P0 protocol; see docs/opendoge_multiskill.md section 5.5

sota_adoption_rule: Run the reference protocol with seeds 0, 1 and 2.

Reject if any per-skill metric is worse than the reference by more than the measured seed spread: walk velocity error > 0.06, handstand < 0.95, getup < 0.93, jump recovery < 0.96, jump peak outside 0.070-0.080 m.
Replace only if it also improves the transition aggregate to >= 0.95, or lifts handstand->walk to >= 0.75 while holding the aggregate >= 0.928.
A better single-seed aggregate is not sufficient on its own: the seed spread alone is 0.928-0.943.

rejected.PPO fine-tune LR 5e-5: 900 iterations; transitions 0.865, walk velocity error 0.054 -> 0.296, handstand -11 points
rejected.recover-to-walk expert (withdrawn): transitions 0.846, handstand->walk 0.760 -> 0.327, jump->handstand 0.969 -> 0.370. Root cause: shared-trunk interference.

selection: Single policy covering walk / handstand / getup / jump with a 54-field observation (48 shared proprioceptive fields + one-hot skill + phase). Adopted as SOTA on the reference protocol above; observation-noise robustness, the full training condition and evaluation-seed variance were all measured before adoption (docs/opendoge_multiskill.md sections 5.5 and 5.6).
